name: insolvia-workspace
//: Root of the Insolvia npm workspace. NOT a shippable package — it declares
the members and pins the shared toolchain.
The member list is EXPLICIT and must stay that way — never `packages/*`.
apps/insolvia_marketing is deliberately NOT a member: it consumes
@insolvia-ai/design-system BY PUBLISHED VERSION from GitHub Packages, never
by path. Globbing (or adding it) would symlink it to local source, so a
broken package would pass CI and only fail after publishing.
packages/insolvia_design_system is BOTH a member and published: the app
consumes it by workspace symlink (source), marketing by published version.
Marketing's own lockfile pins the registry copy, so the member symlink
CAUTION — Node resolution walks UP the tree. A missing dependency in
apps/insolvia_marketing can resolve from this root's node_modules and pass
CI, then fail in a clean install. It keeps its own package-lock.json and
its own CI job installs from it, which is what catches this — do not

//tokens: Run with plain `node`, no loader and no build step: Node >=24 strips

//lint: Fans out per member rather than running ESLint once from the root, and
there is deliberately NO `eslint.config.js` at the repo root — the rules
live in `eslint.base.js`, which each member re-exports. ESLint discovers
a flat config by walking UP from its cwd, so a root one is also found by
any subdirectory with its own ESLint setup, once breaking a version-gated
package's own ESLint 8 gate. Read eslint.base.js before changing this.
//app: The app's own scripts (`build`, `web`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`) live in
apps/insolvia_app/package.json and are a contract with app-*.yml. These two
are conveniences for a developer at the repo root: `app` starts the dev
server on port 3000 (the exact-match Cognito origin), `app:build` produces
//ci: The whole local gate: token drift, format, lint, typecheck, test. Mirrors
what the CI workflows run per area, so `npm run ci` green locally is a
fair predictor of a green PR.
scripts.ci: npm run tokens:check && npm run format && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test

//devDependencies: ESLint/Prettier versions match apps/insolvia_marketing deliberately — the
app added in PR 3 is told to match marketing's lint setup, so a second
ESLint major in the repo would be a trap, not a choice.
TypeScript is 5.9 rather than the 7.x line: `erasableSyntaxOnly` (5.8+) is
the feature this workspace depends on, and adopting a rewritten compiler in
the middle of a toolchain migration would confound any failure.
